name: Union Pacific
description: Union Pacific runs the largest US railroad by route in the West: about 52,400 track miles connecting 23 states, hauling grain, coal, chemicals, metals, autos and intermodal containers. Customers pay per carload, so revenue is carloads times average revenue per car, plus fuel surcharges ($2.3B in 2025) and small accessorial and subsidiary (logistics) charges. It earns a 59.8% operating ratio (operating costs as a share of revenue), among the best in freight rail, because it owns its network and prices to its track. Its 2025 revenue was 95% freight ($23.2B of $24.5B), split about a third bulk, a third industrial, and 30% premium (autos and intermodal). The big pending event is the agreed acquisition of Norfolk Southern (one UNP share plus $88.82 cash per NS share), which would create a coast-to-coast railroad if the Surface Transportation Board approves.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge; not re-checked against MSCI/S&P. SEC SIC 4011 (Railroads, Line-Haul Operating).

hq.note: 1400 Douglas Street, Omaha, NE 68179 (FY2025 10-K); owns the 1.2 million sq ft headquarters building

employees.note: Average employees during 2025, FY2025 10-K; 13 major rail unions represent about 83% of the workforce

businessLines.name: Bulk (grain, fertilizer, food & refrigerated, coal & renewables)
businessLines.how: Carload revenue per shipment plus fuel surcharge; volume follows harvests, export demand and power-plant coal burn (coal & renewables +20% in 2025).
businessLines.description: Grain and grain products $3,926M, fertilizer $856M, food & refrigerated $1,018M, coal & renewables $1,786M.

businessLines.name: Industrial (chemicals & plastics, metals & minerals, forest products, energy & specialized)
businessLines.how: Carload revenue tied to industrial production and construction; includes sand, crude and other energy freight.
businessLines.description: Industrial chemicals & plastics $2,512M, metals & minerals $2,193M, forest products $1,290M, energy & specialized markets $2,609M.

businessLines.name: Premium (automotive, intermodal)
businessLines.how: Per-container and per-vehicle revenue; intermodal competes with trucking and depends on import volumes and West Coast ports; revenue fell 2% in 2025.

businessLines.name: Other (subsidiary, accessorial and other revenues)
businessLines.how: Fees for storage, detention and logistics services.
businessLines.description: Other subsidiary revenues $718M (logistics; commuter operations transferred to Metra), accessorial revenues $475M, other $97M.

whatsNext.text: Acquisition of Norfolk Southern: each NS share converts to 1 UNP share plus $88.82 cash; about 225 million UNP shares to be issued and about $20B cash paid, funded by new debt and operating cash. Both shareholder groups approved Nov 14, 2025. STB rejected the first application as incomplete (Jan 16, 2026); a revised application was accepted as complete May 28, 2026 but the proceeding is held in abeyance pending supplemental information due July 27, 2026; first portion filed July 7, 2026
whatsNext.note: Termination fee of $2.5B owed to Norfolk Southern in some circumstances (FY2025 10-K)
